What @GatorJumper said is mostly true. You might find some obscure Silk Road knock off, the occasional conspiracy site, etc. as long as you use a secure browser and sandbox it properly you should be fine as far as viruses go. If you're that worried about it, explore the deep net inside of a virtual machine (I use Hyper-V for this)

Just like everything on the internet, there's good and bad. But when you're browsing stuff like .onion sites with TOR, you have to know what you're looking for. You won't accidentally stumble across something illegal. Just keep in mind the shit you'll see that is clandestine (hackers for hire, hitmen, murder livestreams, etc) is almost all fake. The TOR browser bundle is relatively secure, but if you want to make sure nothing touches your computer, look up TAILS and how to put it on a flash drive or DVD. It has all the software you need to access hidden sites while also being completely separate from your hard drive.

Edit: Also, a lot of people on YouTube will show it off as some kinda shady dark corner of the internet filled with hackers and what not. This simply isn't true. It's mostly websites that host illegal content in their countries (pirated ebooks and what not), places where anonymity is desired like imageboards, and mirrors of popular websites like Wikipedia
